head: claude/work-digest-empty-body
title: notify: the ping body was silently dropped, and the digest measured the wrong thing
body:
Two defects on the **operator notification path** — the mechanism by which the operator is told what was done without them, and so the condition the whole autonomy grant rests on. A digest that fires and says nothing is worse than one that does not fire, because it looks like oversight happened.

Reported first-hand: the last thing the ClaudeBot channel received was a 03:24 message reading, in its entirety, `work_digest`.

---

## Tier — established, not assumed

**Tier 1.** `notify_on_pull.py` does execute on the money box (invoked by `scripts/deploy_pull_restart.sh`, triggered by `deploy/ict-git-sync.service`), so "it's observability" is not by itself sufficient — that is why this is argued rather than asserted.

**What it does NOT touch:** no order path, no `RiskManager`, no `config/`, no account mode, no strategy or risk parameter, no systemd unit, no service restart, no `src/runtime/*`, no DB write. It cannot place, modify, cancel, or refuse a trade. Both changed files are read-only with respect to every trading surface.

**What it DOES touch, on the live VM:** the text of a Telegram message, and one append to a JSONL queue in the repo working tree. The blast radius of getting it wrong is a mis-worded or duplicated ping — which is exactly the failure mode being repaired, and the change is monotone in the safe direction (see the byte-identical proof).

The one genuine risk is that this path also carries **CRITICAL safety pages** (unprotected position, over-cover, close failure). That is why the byte-identical proof below is over the real committed queue rather than over invented fixtures, and why the empty-row behaviour was chosen to fail *loud and delivered* rather than *silent and dropped*.

---

## DEFECT 1 — the body was silently dropped

### Reproduced first

The exact row shape `work_digest.py` writes, through the current `origin/main` renderer:

```
$ python3 -c "... from notify_on_pull import _render_event_body ..."
=== RENDERED (repr) ===
'work_digest'
```

The label, and nothing else. `_render_ping_message`/`_render_event_body` assembled the body from a **fixed list of CONTENT keys** — `cp_id, next_cp, phase, strategy, model, result, grade, question, summary` plus head and URL keys. `"message"` is on none of them.

### It was never a `work_digest` problem

**MEASURED** over the committed queue file `docs/claude/pending-pings.jsonl` (population: **all 50 rows**, read 2026-09-02):

| | |
|---|--:|
| rows rendering to **nothing but their event label** | **21 of 50 (42%)** |
| distinct event types affected | `health-review` ×6, `performance-review` ×6, `ml-review` ×5, `ping` ×2, `session-wrap` ×1, `work_digest` ×1 |
| producers writing `"message"` | **2** — `scripts/ops/work_phase_ping.py` (Phase A) and `scripts/ops/work_digest.py` (Phase B) |

So **every review-session ping the operator has ever been sent arrived as a bare label too.** The channel has been substantially mute, not just last night.

### Why not "add `message` to the list"

Because that is the same hand-maintained list one entry longer, and the next producer that picks a different key fails identically and just as silently. It has already failed for two producers and five event types. This repo made exactly that call three days ago on `LIVE_BACKLOGS` (#10725): refuse the one-entry fix, *pin* the coverage so it cannot fall behind.

### The choice: render-unknown, **and** a loud floor under it

Both, layered — and the layering is the point, because each alone leaves a hole.

**1. Invert which list is hand-maintained.** The old design hand-maintained the **CONTENT** keys, which is an *open* set: it grows with every producer, and getting it wrong loses a message silently. The new design hand-maintains the **ENVELOPE** — `at`, `reviewed_at`, `target`, `priority`, `event` — which is *closed*: it is exactly what this transport itself sets or consumes (`send_ping.enqueue(body, priority, target)` plus the row timestamp and the discriminator). It cannot grow without a change to the transport.

The failure directions are opposite, and that is the whole argument:

| a key nobody listed | old design | new design |
|---|---|---|
| new **content** key | **message silently lost** | it renders |
| new **envelope** key | — | one metadata line leaks into the channel |

A leaked internal key is visible, cosmetic and self-announcing. A lost message is none of those. That is the trade this accepts, deliberately — and yes, it means keys like `digest_state` now render. Good: that is the collapsed-state grading, and the operator should see it.

Rendering keys on the *shape of the value* rather than a list of names: a **multi-line string is prose** and renders bare; any other scalar renders `key: value`; a container renders as truncated JSON. No name list anywhere in that rule.

**2. A genuinely body-less row fails LOUD, and is still delivered.** This is bar 3, and the direction is argued rather than defaulted.

The alternative was to **refuse to enqueue**. Refusal is loud at enqueue time — but enqueue time is inside `notify_on_pull.py` on the live VM, where "loud" means `logger.error` into journald. This repo has measured, repeatedly, that journald is where an alarm goes to be unread: the IB over-cover and Bybit over-cover pages both detected correctly *for weeks* and reached nobody, because `logger.error` never touches `outcomes.jsonl` and so never touches Telegram, the notifications banner, or `/api/bot/logs`. **Refusing would have moved the silent drop from the renderer into journald — the third silent drop, wearing a different hat.**

So the row is sent and announces its own emptiness:

```
work_digest
⚠️ EMPTY PING — this row carried no renderable content (keys: at, event,
priority, target). That is a PRODUCER defect, not a quiet day: something
queued a notification with nothing in it.
```

The operator learns a ping fired with nothing to say — a defect report they can act on. They never receive a confident bare label that looks like oversight happened.

### The docstring

It asserted *"Unknown events fall back to the raw event name as the label so nothing is silently dropped"* — true of the LABEL, false of the BODY, and a comment promising a guarantee the code does not provide is how the next reader stops looking. Rewritten to state what the code now actually does, with the failure it used to have named.

### Byte-identical proof

Rendered **every row in the live committed queue** through the `origin/main` renderer and the new one, and diffed:

```
n=50   byte-identical=29   newly-rendered (previously bare label)=21   PERTURBED=0
```

Zero rows that rendered correctly before render differently now. Nothing on the CRITICAL-page path moves.

⚠️ **This proof caught a real bug in my own fix.** The first draft counted only body/URL keys as "content" and forgot that `sprint`/`title` land on the *head* line — so every well-formed `sprint-start` row (label + sprint + title, nothing else) tripped the empty-ping notice. Nine rows perturbed. Review did not catch it; the arithmetic did. Pinned by `test_a_row_with_only_a_title_is_not_treated_as_empty`.

---

## DEFECT 2 — the content, which is the worse half

It measured the **work STORE** and reported that as **the WORK**. Nothing that happened last night moves a `lifecycle:` field in `docs/claude/work/objects/*.yaml`, so even with Defect 1 fixed the operator would have received a confident report that nothing happened.

### What it does now

It diffs **six keyed-item registers** across the same two git refs — no new state file, nothing to fall out of sync:

`docs/claude/work/MANAGER-CHECKLIST.json` · `docs/claude/OPEN-ITEMS.json` · the four `docs/claude/*-review-backlog.json`.

**Not a PR counter, structurally.** Only a change to a declared **STATE FIELD** is an event — a checklist item reaching `done`/`blocked`/`landed_unproven`, a register row filed or CLEARED, a backlog row given a terminal disposition. An edit that closes nothing is invisible *by construction*, not by a heuristic over diff text. `queued` and `triage` are deliberately **not** checklist events: scoping is activity. Backlog **filings** are counted, never enumerated — the verdict is the event, the filing is not. Merged PRs sit on the **population line as attribution and a denominator**, never the headline; a test asserts the PR count is not on the headline line *and* that it is still reported.

Enumeration is capped and prioritised: only **what is waiting on a human** and **what a register stopped watching** get listed by id. The acceptance-case output is 22 lines, and a test fails it above 30.

### Acceptance case

**The literal range `a9444bc6..34f2beb5` is not resolvable** — `34f2beb5` is in neither this clone nor `origin` (`git fetch origin 34f2beb5` → `couldn't find remote ref`). That is not a workaround, it is the design working:

```
[work digest] 2026-09-02
⚠️ window NOT examined — ref '34f2beb5' is not in this clone (shallow). This is
'we could not look', NOT 'nothing changed'.
No register was read (6 declared). Nothing below describes the window you asked about.
```

So here is the same night over the window that **is** resolvable, `1bae542a..d06cd3e9` (00:36→07:33, the merge burst).

**Before — the entire message:**
```
No lifecycle change in a9444bc6..34f2beb5 (population: 584 work objects).
```

**After:**
```
[work digest] 2026-09-02
52 state change(s) across 6/6 registers read + the work store.
Window 1bae542a..d06cd3e9 — 49 commits / 49 merged PRs; 584 work objects; 6/6 registers read.
manager checklist: 14 landed_unproven · 6 done · 4 blocked · 3 in_flight · 7 filed
open-items register: 6 filed · 1 CLEARED
health backlog: 6 resolved · 28 filed
performance backlog: 4 resolved · 2 filed
ml backlog: 1 filed
research backlog: 5 resolved
work store: 3 lifecycle change(s):
  • WO-20260901-PHASE-D: dormant → waiting · Phase D — the constraint, computed rather than judged
  • WO-20260901-PHASE-G: dormant → in_flight · Phase G — the forcing function — retirement, and the E2 pull rule
  • WO-20260901-PHASE-H: dormant → in_flight · Phase H — the control half — decisions from the UI, and the read gate
NEEDS YOU / CHANGED WATCH:
  ⛔ MI-23-PHASE-G-ASKS-THE-OPERATOR-FOR-THREE-RETIREMENT-DECISIONS: blocked — The first sunset pass produced evidenced candidates; three need an operator call
  ⛔ MI-25-FULL-TRADING-HISTORY-IS-WORLD-READABLE-UNAUTHENTICATED: blocked — The Data Explorer serves the live journal to anyone on the public Caddy host
  ⛔ MI-29-LEGS-ARE-STARVED-BY-SIBLINGS-ON-ONE-NETTED-SYMBOL: blocked — A better explanation for the never-traded legs than 'long-horizon'
  ⛔ MI-34-SHOULD-A-CONFIRMED-VENUE-WEDGE-KEEP-PAGING-FOREVER: blocked — Operator decision requested on #10679: page severity for an unclearable broker wedge
  ✔ OI-20260830-BYBIT-HEDGE-MODE-ARMED-BUT-UNEXERCISED: CLEARED — Bybit HEDGE position mode is now live on ALL EIGHT (account, symbol) pairs
Standing: dormant 576 / ready 0 / in_flight 4 / waiting 4 / done 0 / accepted 0 / unknown 0 (of 584)
WIP 4/8 in flight (enforced_in_ci — this IS a gate: the ninth is refused).
Waiting: WO-20260901-PHASE-A, WO-20260901-PHASE-B, WO-20260901-PHASE-C, WO-20260901-PHASE-D
⚠️ Work store covers the operating-layer build's own phases — the carried backlog rows: Phase C — COMPLETE 2026-09-01. Registers above are read too, but this is still NOT the whole of system work.
```

It names the two retired backlog classes as **15 rows given a terminal disposition** across three backlogs, the cleared monitoring row by id, and **four things blocked on the operator** — including one that had no other route to them. The narrow range the report used (`a9444bc6..d06cd3e9`, 2 commits) now reads `1 done · 1 landed_unproven` instead of "No lifecycle change".

### "Nothing changed" vs "could not look" — now distinguishable at two levels

**Per source**, three grades, never collapsed:

- `read` — parsed.
- `absent` — the register does not exist at that ref. **An observation:** we looked and it is not there.
- `unreadable` — it exists and would not parse. **We did not look.** Renders as `⚠️ <name>: UNREADABLE — we could not look. Nothing about it below is an observation.`

**Per digest**, `digestState` gains a fourth state — `sources_unreadable`, for a resolved window where *not one* register could be read. Only `unreadable` may downgrade the digest; treating `absent` as "could not look" would make every fresh checkout report a broken window.

**A partially-read window says so rather than reading as clean:**
```
No state change in <a>..<b> across the 4 register(s) read. ⚠️ 2 of 6 NOT READ —
see below; this is not a clean night, it is a partial one.
```

`sourceReads` ships on **every** digest including the unresolved envelope (as `not_attempted`), because a key that vanishes makes a consumer branch on absence, and absence is not one of the states.

One more collapse closed: a register **created inside the window** is flagged `firstSeen` and **not diffed** — otherwise every row it has ever held reads as "new tonight", a loud lie.

---

## Verification

| | |
|---|---|
| Defect 1 reproduced against `origin/main` before fixing | ✅ shown above |
| Byte-identical over the live queue (n=50) | ✅ **29 identical / 21 newly rendered / 0 perturbed** |
| Empty row fails loud **and delivered** | ✅ `test_a_body_less_row_announces_itself_rather_than_arriving_blank` |
| `scripts/ci/run_guards.py` **after the final commit** | ✅ **PASS 47 · FAIL 0 · SKIP 23** |
| `ruff check` (pinned `>=0.15,<0.16`, as CI runs it) | ✅ clean |
| `pytest tests/test_work_digest.py tests/test_notify_render_no_silent_drop.py tests/test_notify_on_pull.py` | ✅ **88 passed** |
| `work_digest.py --self-test` | ✅ 12/12 |

⚠️ **On the guards run:** the first pass reported `PASS 46 · FAIL 1`, with `layer-guard` failing `exit 127` — `lint-imports` was simply not installed in this sandbox. That is *"could not measure"*, not a finding. I installed `import-linter` and ran it directly (`Contracts: 6 kept, 0 broken`) before re-running the suite clean. Recording it rather than quietly reporting the second number.

⚠️ **One pre-existing test failure, not caused by this PR:** `test_digest_and_route_publish_the_same_ceiling_facts` fails with `ModuleNotFoundError: fastapi` in this sandbox. Verified pre-existing by `git stash` + re-run on the unmodified tree, and it passes once `fastapi` is installed.

**No test or guard was weakened.** One existing test changed — `test_identical_refs_are_no_changes_which_is_a_real_observation` asserted `"No lifecycle change" in render(d)`, which was exactly the sentence the digest had no business saying. The replacement is **stronger**: it requires the quiet-window claim to carry the denominator of what was actually examined (`"register(s) read"`). The rename rationale is in the test docstring.

**15 new tests** in `tests/test_notify_render_no_silent_drop.py` + 16 appended to `tests/test_work_digest.py`, including a positive control that reconstructs the pre-fix key list and *proves it drops the body* — a probe that cannot find the positive proves nothing about the fix.

### Both coverage lists are pinned, not trusted

- `ENVELOPE_KEYS` is pinned against `inspect.signature(send_ping.enqueue)` — a key belongs there only if the transport actually consumes it — plus a size bound, so it cannot quietly grow into a dumping ground that hides content.
- Every row in the **live committed queue** must render to more than a bare label. That test fails the moment a producer appends a row the renderer cannot say anything about.
- `SOURCES` is pinned against `docs/claude/*-review-backlog.json` **on disk** — self-test 11 fails if a review backlog exists that the digest never reads. This is the `LIVE_BACKLOGS` lesson applied: a hand-maintained coverage list that can fall behind unnoticed *is* the defect.

---

## FOR THE MANAGER

**Deployment.** Defect 1's fix only takes effect on the live VM once `ict-git-sync` pulls it; until then every queued ping still arrives as a bare label. **Nothing has been observed on the fleet** — this is `landed_unproven` at best, and the observation that would clear it is: a real `work_digest` (or any `message`-keyed) ping arriving in `@ict_cluade_bot` **with a body**. Note `OI-20260901-CLAUDE-CHANNEL-SEPARATION-SHIPPED-BUT-UNPROVEN` is open on the same channel, so a delivered ping is not yet proof it went to the *right* chat.

**Backlog rows to place** (I did not touch the backlogs — three sessions are live on other files):

1. **`BL-20260902-PING-RENDERER-DROPPED-42PCT-OF-QUEUED-BODIES`** — severity `high`, tier `1`, status `resolved` by this PR. *Population: all 50 rows in `docs/claude/pending-pings.jsonl`, read 2026-09-02 — 21 (42%) rendered to nothing but their event label, across 5 event types and 2 producers. The whole review-session ping channel (`health-review` ×6, `performance-review` ×6, `ml-review` ×5) was mute for its entire life.* Resolution criteria: a real `message`-keyed ping observed arriving with a body, on the fleet, not in a test.

2. **`BL-20260902-WORK-DIGEST-MEASURED-THE-STORE-AND-REPORTED-IT-AS-THE-WORK`** — severity `high`, tier `1`, status `resolved` by this PR. *Over `1bae542a..d06cd3e9` (49 commits / 49 merged PRs, 15 backlog rows closed, 1 register row cleared, 4 items blocked on the operator) the digest emitted "No lifecycle change".* Resolution criteria: a scheduled (`event=schedule`) `work-digest` run whose committed row carries a non-empty per-register summary.

3. **`BL-20260902-DOCSTRING-ASSERTED-A-SAFETY-PROPERTY-THE-CODE-LACKED`** — severity `medium`, tier `1`, status `resolved` by this PR. *`_render_event_body`'s docstring claimed "nothing is silently dropped" — true of the label, false of the body — for the entire period the body was being dropped. The class is worth a row of its own: a comment promising a guarantee is what makes the next reader stop looking.* Resolution criteria: n/a (class record).

**Two things I found and did NOT fix, deliberately out of scope:**

- `scripts/ops/work_phase_ping.py` writes the same `"message"` key. It is **fixed by this change** (the renderer no longer drops it) and I did not edit the file, so no conflict with any live session.
- **`docs/claude/pending-pings.jsonl` holds 21 rows that will now render differently if they are ever re-drained.** They will not be: the VM-local `runtime_logs/pending_pings_delivered.txt` ledger dedupes on the raw line hash. But if that VM is ever re-provisioned, the ledger is gone (it is `.gitignore`d) and those 21 old pings will re-fire — *now with bodies*. That risk pre-dates this PR; this change alters what they would say, not whether they fire. Worth a manager decision on whether to prune the file.

**Not a merge request.** DRAFT, per the brief. I hold no merge slot and have posted no claim.
